title: metsuke v1 — SPO telemetry build
description:
Build epic for the metsuke v1 telemetry pipeline: SPO agent (scrape, spool, sign, upload) and ingest server (verify, archive to S3), per /tmp/metsuke-spec.md collapsed from wayfinder map musashi-ping-sak (decision phase; all 15 map tickets closed). Decision detail lives in musashi-ping-sak.1–15 and docs/research/; accepted decisions in docs/adr/0001–0007. Scaffolding is done and green — tickets start from a working workspace.

## Success Criteria

- An SPO can follow the instructions page from zero to verified uploads: static binary, hardened unit, cold-key or Calidus signing.
- The server verifies, replay-protects, and archives every accepted submission raw in S3; the index is rebuildable from a bucket listing.
- nix flake check stays hermetic and green; the VM test proves the full path on hydraJobs.

Review of the uncommitted tree implementing .19 .21 .24 .25 .26 .28 .29 .31 .32 .33 .34 .35. No untracked files.

- `src/s3.rs:104-107` — comment claims "an answer ... that is not UTF-8" errors. ureq 3.4.0 `Body::read_to_string` sets `lossy_utf8(true)`, so it never does; the bytes are decoded with replacement chars instead. The `BodyExceedsLimit` half is correct. Fix: drop the UTF-8 clause.

The test cannot distinguish "rejected as misplaced" from "rejected as unknown", so it would not catch the flag regressing to unparsed. Fix: assert on `"only means anything to"`.
- `cli.rs:53-54` says "The flag may be written either side of the subcommand word", but only `rebuild-index --allow-empty` is exercised (`tests/binary.rs:594`). The reversed order is a claim no artifact holds. Fix: add `[ALLOW_EMPTY, REBUILD_INDEX]` to `rebuild_index_on_an_archive_with_nothing_in_it_exits_nonzero`, or a unit test on `Args::parse`.
- `rebuild.rs:48-53` — `RebuildError::Empty` names neither the archive root nor the bucket, yet `EmptyArchive`'s own doc says the case it guards is "a mistyped or unmounted `archive.root`". The operator is asked to decide wrong-path vs really-empty and given nothing to decide on. CLAUDE.md: a message naming what failed and what it got. Fix: `Empty { archive: String }`, filled from the root path or `bucket`.
- `config.rs:54` — `put_retries` is the only numeric field left plain `u32`, and the reason zero is legitimate there lives solely in `tests/config.rs:184`. The module header at `config.rs:1-4` says every field where zero means nothing is a `NonZero`, so a reader at the field cannot tell exception from oversight. Fix: state it in the field's doc comment.

## Prose

- `tests/binary.rs:555-556` — near-verbatim copy of `cli.rs:24-27` ("accepting it there would read as though it did something"), introduced by the round-1 fix. `cli.rs` owns it; the test doc should state the case only.
- `contrib/server.example.toml:3-5` — "What each value means is the doc comment on its field in `crates/metsuke-server/src/config.rs`" is false for `bucket` and `region` (`config.rs:41-42`) and `rate_limit_window_secs` (`:91`), which carry no doc comment. Fix the three docs, or soften the pointer.
- `contrib/server.example.toml` — four clauses still duplicate their owner: `:1-2` "nothing here has a default" (`config.rs:1-2`), `:10-12` trailing "which is what keeps this file Nix-managed and public" (`config.rs:35-37`, word for word), `:31-32` "as the allowlist admin command generates them" (`config.rs:79-81`), `:24-25` "so `verify-archive` cannot run against it" (`main.rs:85-87` and `Fatal::CannotVerifyFilesystem`). The env var names at `:10-11` are the example's own and should stay.

## Standards and reuse

- `cli.rs:73,86-90` — `Command::RebuildIndex { allow_empty: false }` is built with a placeholder inside the loop and patched by a second match after it, so the flag is held in two representations and `false` reads the same as a decision. No behaviour bug at any argument ordering (checked bare, both orders, `verify-archive --allow-empty`, two subcommands, repeated subcommand). The fix is strictly smaller code: keep only `named` in the loop, build `Command` once afterwards from `(named.as_deref(), allow_empty)`, and return `AllowEmptyWithoutRebuild` from the non-rebuild arms. Deletes the `taken`/`command` pair and the fix-up match.
- `tests/config.rs:70-88` — `without` and `with` each re-derive `format!("{field} =")` and the same lines/filter/join walk. Fix: one `edited(field, Option<&str>)` where `None` drops the line, or share an `assigns(line, field)` predicate.
- `tests/s3.rs:206-212` — `stored(counter, wire_bytes, signature)` forwards to `stored_submission(key, counter, timestamp, signature, wire_bytes)` with the last two arguments swapped. It compiles only because the types differ. Fix: match the helper's order, or delete the forwarder and call `stored_submission` at the four sites.

title: Envelope and Ed25519 sign/verify core
description:
## What to build

The shared wire contract both crates trust: envelope types (schema_version starting at 1, pool_id, agent_version, replay counter, timestamp, samples with the 8 nullable v1 fields), zstd compression, and raw detached Ed25519 sign/verify over the compressed body bytes (ADR 0001). Exposed as a library from the metsuke crate so the server consumes the identical types and defaults — reviewers verify one definition, not two copies.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Property test: envelope encode→decode roundtrip.
- [ ] Property test: sign→verify roundtrip, and any tampered byte in the compressed body rejects.
- [ ] Replay counter and timestamp sit inside the signed payload (ADR 0002).
- [ ] metsuke-server can depend on the metsuke crate as a library.

## Blocked by

None — can start immediately.
close_reason: seal/open wire core with property tests; flake check green

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Shipped: envelope schema v1 (PoolId opaque type, 8 nullable sample fields) with seal/open as the whole wire interface — seal = JSON+zstd+Ed25519 sign, open = verify_strict before bounded decompress (ADR 0001/0002). Property tests: seal→open roundtrip, tamper rejects, PoolId bech32 roundtrip; unit tests for size cap, NaN, malformed/wrong-prefix/wrong-length pool ids. Server depends on metsuke by path; crate versions decoupled per ADR 0006. Filed metsuke-9a1 (deferred metsuke-wire extraction).

title: Developer data endpoints
description:
## What to build

Developer pull access to the archive without per-dev AWS credentials: a single basic-auth user (credentials via sops EnvironmentFile), a listing route (prefix and after filters, JSON from the SQLite index) and a download route streaming the raw S3 object. Read-only, no transformation — developers get the same self-verifying bytes the bucket holds.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Missing or wrong credentials → 401 on both routes.
- [ ] Listing filters by prefix and after; results come from the index, not a live bucket scan.
- [ ] Download streams the object byte-identical to what was archived.

## Blocked by

S3 storage implementation and rebuildable index.

title: Instructions page
description:
## What to build

The SPO onboarding surface: one static HTML page (no JS, no CSS effort) rendered at server build time from a template whose every code-owned value — intervals, port, flake output names, latest client version, the exact field list that leaves the box — is pulled from the client crate at compile, so documentation can never drift from shipped defaults (ADR 0006). Outline per musashi-ping-sak.14: intro and fields, register, choose signing key, enable PrometheusSimple, install, configure, systemd, verify, staying up to date. Numbered copy-paste steps take an SPO from zero to verified uploads.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Page builds from client-crate constants; changing a default in code changes the page with no manual edit.
- [ ] The exact v1 field list appears on the page.
- [ ] All outline sections present, each step copy-pasteable.
- [ ] Served by the ingest server as static content.

## Blocked by

Client binary end-to-end; Server ingest pipeline, cold-key path.

title: Static builds, NixOS modules, hardened unit
description:
## What to build

Distribution as declared in the spec — Nix-flake-only, no install script ever: static musl flake outputs metsuke-static-x86_64-linux and metsuke-static-aarch64-linux cross-built via crane, a NixOS module for the agent and one for the server (all spec limits exposed as module options, never hardcoded), and an example hardened unit at contrib/metsuke.service (DynamicUser, ProtectSystem=strict, StateDirectory, no groups — ADR 0007) with the LoadCredential variant documented as optional.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both static outputs build; binaries link no dynamic libraries.
- [ ] Agent module renders config TOML from options; server module exposes every limit as an option.
- [ ] contrib unit committed; agent runs under it against a loopback endpoint with no extra privileges.
- [ ] nix flake check remains hermetic and green.

## Blocked by

Client binary end-to-end.

title: Server SQLite backup timer
description:
## What to build

Recovery for the index between rebuilds: a systemd timer in the server NixOS module running roughly hourly — sqlite3 .backup, zstd, aws s3 cp into a backups/ prefix in the same bucket, using the server's existing scoped credentials. Complements (does not replace) the rebuild-from-listing path.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Timer and service rendered by the server module; cadence is an option.
- [ ] Backup is a consistent snapshot (sqlite3 .backup, not a file copy), compressed, uploaded under backups/.
- [ ] Failure surfaces in the journal; it never blocks ingest.

## Blocked by

Static builds, NixOS modules, hardened unit.

title: NixOS VM end-to-end test
description:
## What to build

The one non-hermetic sanity gate (hydraJobs only, never in nix flake check): a NixOS VM test wiring a real idle Leios node (pinned via the ouroboros-leios prototype tag input, not capkgs), the real agent via its module, the real server via its module, and Garage as S3. Asserts the full path — scrape → spool → signed upload → verify → S3 object → ACK — once; moving values stay covered by tier-2 fixtures.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] VM test passes: an object appears in Garage and the agent logs the ACK.
- [ ] Runs from hydraJobs; excluded from nix flake check (which stays no-node, no-VM, no-network).
- [ ] Leios pin is a flake input, bumpable with the fixture re-record flow.

## Blocked by

S3 storage implementation and rebuildable index; Static builds, NixOS modules, hardened unit.

title: Bucket and IAM in cardano-playground
description:
## What to build

External-repo infrastructure (cardano-playground, not this repo): the cardano-playground-metsuke bucket in the opentofu bootstrap (SSE-KMS via the shared key alias, versioning, TLS-only policy, access logging, public access blocked) and the IT-security-approved dedicated IAM user — PutObject/GetObject/ListBucket on this one bucket plus KMS decrypt/generate scoped to the alias — with static keys in a sops EnvironmentFile readable only by the metsuke systemd user on the db-sync host. Blocks production deploy only; the VM test uses Garage and does not wait on this.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Bucket applied with all five protections listed above.
- [ ] IAM policy grants nothing beyond the one bucket and the scoped KMS actions.
- [ ] Credentials land via sops, readable only by the service user.

## Blocked by

None — can start immediately (gates production deploy, not other tickets).

title: HTTP ingest endpoint and server binary wiring
description:
crates/metsuke-server/src/main.rs is still `println!("metsuke-server")`. Nothing loads IngestConfig (no TOML/env loader), binds a socket, or constructs Intake.

Needs: config load, listener, POST route reading the ADR-0001 headers into Submission, and the status mapping IngestError already implies — IngestError::Rejected -> 4xx with the Rejection text, CounterState/Archive -> 5xx (ADR 0004, so the client keeps spooling).

metsuke-4zo.6 delivered the intake library; .7 assumes a 503 path exists. No ticket owned this layer.
close_reason: HTTP ingest endpoint, config loader, and server binary wiring

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
## Review — HTTP ingest endpoint and server binary wiring

### Silent failures

- `src/http.rs:249-259` — `serve()` treats a dead listener as a dropped connection. tiny_http 0.12 pushes `Message::Error` and `break`s out of its accept thread when `accept()` fails (lib.rs:341-345), so `recv()` yields that error exactly once and every later call blocks forever on an empty queue. The process stays alive, logs `dropped a connection` once, and accepts nothing again; systemd sees a healthy unit. Fix: make `serve` return `Result<Infallible, io::Error>`, propagate the recv error to `main`, exit nonzero.
- `src/http.rs:249-339` — nothing bounds how long a body read may take, and the loop is single-threaded, so one client that sends headers then stalls wedges ingest for every pool. `read_body` bounds size, not time. Fix: set a read timeout on the connection, or state in the module header that the fronting proxy must fully buffer request bodies and file that requirement against the NixOS module ticket (metsuke-4zo.12).

### Prose claims

- `src/http.rs:1-4` — "any IP-level limit belong to the reverse proxy … see docs/research/endpoint-protection.md §4". §4 is Transport (TLS only); IP and rate limiting are §3 step 3 and §5. Fix: cite §3 and §5 for the limit half of the claim.
- `src/http.rs:225-227` — retells ADR-0004 and drifts from it: the comment calls 4xx "permanent", ADR-0004 says on 4xx the client keeps the data spooled and retries with clamped exponential backoff. Fix: cut to a pointer, `// Status family only; ADR 0004 defines what each means to the client.`
- `src/config.rs:92-93` — "The S3 archive (ticket metsuke-4zo.7) replaces it" is a third copy; `src/archive.rs:1-3` and `:12-13` already own that fact. Fix: drop the ticket clause.

### Ambiguity

Ticket says "no TOML/env loader"; only TOML is loaded. Was an env source required, or was that phrasing just naming what was absent?

### Gates run this session

`cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features` — clean. `cargo test` — 100 passed, 0 failed (11 in metsuke-server/tests/binary.rs, 9 in tests/http.rs, 4 in tests/config.rs). `nix flake check` not run.

### Beads hygiene

No untracked files; every change is staged. `br sync --status`: in sync, 0 dirty. Ticket has no resolution comment and is still in_progress — yours to close. Map metsuke-4zo has no Decisions/Out-of-scope sections, so nothing to update there.

### Filed

Commented on metsuke-9a1 (cross-crate duplication: ERR/WARNING/INFO, `hex`, three hex decoders, the `Args::parse` loop).

### Verdict

Not ready for /commit: the listener-death path and the missing body-read bound need a decision first. The three prose fixes are cheap.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
## Review 2 — HTTP ingest endpoint and server binary wiring

All five findings from the first review are addressed: `serve` returns `Result<Infallible, io::Error>` and `main` exits FAILURE; the body-timeout requirement is documented in the http.rs header and filed as metsuke-a3a; the endpoint-protection citation now names sections that exist; the ADR-0004 retelling is a pointer; the 4zo.7 clause is gone from config.rs.

### Correctness

- `src/http.rs:read_body` — the Content-Length shortcut does not avoid the cost it claims to. Refusing without reading leaves the remainder for tiny_http's `EqualReader::drop`, which allocates `vec![0; declared_content_length]` on the serving thread. Measured: one header-only POST declaring `Content-Length: 4000000000`, answered 400, took the process from VmSize 347544 kB to 4253796 kB. Detail and the fix are on metsuke-a3a. In this diff, fix the comment: the check saves verification work, not reading.

### Prose claims

- `src/http.rs` `decode_hex` doc — "ADR 0001 fixes what the client emits" is not in ADR 0001, which says only that "HTTP headers carry pool id, verification key, and signature" and specifies no hex encoding or casing. What actually fixes it is `crates/metsuke/src/uploader.rs` `fn hex` (lowercase). Fix: name that, drop the ADR citation.

### Logging

- `src/http.rs:respond` and `refuse` — a failed `respond` is logged at WARNING and dropped. tiny_http already maps BrokenPipe/ConnectionReset to `Ok`, so what reaches this branch is a real write failure on a submission already archived with its counter spent: the agent never sees the ACK, resends, and gets 400 `does not advance`. Neither line names the pool. Fix: log this one at ERR, and put the claimed pool id in both messages.

### Open question

Ticket says "no TOML/env loader"; only TOML is loaded. Was an env source required, or was that phrasing naming what was absent? Asked in review 1, unanswered.

### Gates run this session

`cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features` — clean. `cargo test --workspace` — 100 passed, 0 failed. `nix flake check` not run.

### Beads hygiene

No untracked files; every change staged. Ticket still in_progress with no resolution comment — yours to close. Map metsuke-4zo has no Decisions/Out-of-scope sections. The cross-crate duplication (ERR/WARNING/INFO, `hex`, three hex decoders, the `Args::parse` loop) is already on metsuke-9a1 from review 1; re-confirmed, nothing new to file. `.beads/issues.jsonl` needs re-staging after this flush.

### Verdict

Three fixes, all small and none blocking a decision: the read_body comment, the ADR-0001 hex citation, and the respond/refuse log level and pool id.

title: spool migrate() silently opens a future schema
description:
crates/metsuke/src/spool.rs:57 — `.skip(applied as usize)` yields an empty iterator when user_version > MIGRATIONS.len(), so migrate() returns Ok and an old binary runs against a schema it does not know.

Fix: error when applied > MIGRATIONS.len(), naming both numbers.

Pre-existing; the same hole was copied into crates/metsuke-server/src/counters.rs by metsuke-4zo.6 and is fixed there in scope.
close_reason: Fixed by the shared metsuke::sqlite::migrate guard

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Fixed in metsuke-4zo.6: migrate() moved to metsuke::sqlite with the applied > migrations.len() guard, so spool.rs and the server counter store share it. Covered by metsuke-server/tests/counters.rs a_database_from_a_newer_build_fails_loudly. Close with .6's commit.

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Implemented by metsuke-4zo.6's diff: crates/metsuke/src/sqlite.rs:21-26 refuses a database whose user_version exceeds the migration list (MigrateError::FromTheFuture), and both spool.rs and counters.rs now call that shared migrate(). Close this once .6 lands.

title: scrape test races for a released MockServer port
description:
crates/metsuke/tests/scrape.rs:77 `unreachable_endpoint_yields_all_nulls` starts a MockServer, drops it, and assumes the port stays dead. Another test's MockServer takes the freed port and serves a chain body, so the sample comes back populated.

Observed red in 2 of 4 runs on the metsuke-4zo.6 tree (`cargo test --workspace` and `nix flake check`, one each); both retries passed.

Fix: point at an address nothing can reclaim (RFC 5737 TEST-NET-1, as tests/uploader.rs does) instead of racing for a released one.
close_reason: unreachable scrape test now targets TEST-NET-1 instead of a reclaimable port

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Reproduces on the metsuke-4zo.6 working tree, not a one-off: 2 of 4 runs red this session. `cargo test --workspace` failed it once then passed 84/0; `nix flake check` failed it once (node_version/node_revision came back populated from another test's MockServer) then passed. It is the only thing standing between this tree and a green gate — worth raising from P3.

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Replaced the released-MockServer-port trick with 192.0.2.1:9 (TEST-NET-1) and a 200ms timeout in unreachable_endpoint_yields_all_nulls. cargo test --workspace green x3; nix flake check: all checks passed.

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Superseded by .42: MetricsUrl refuses off-host addresses, so 192.0.2.1 is no longer constructible. tests/scrape.rs now uses 127.0.0.1:9. The race this ticket fixed does not return — port 9 is privileged and MockServer binds ephemeral ports — but the close reason above names an address the code now rejects.

title: Archive trait conflates store and list, forcing unreachable!() in every double
description:
crates/metsuke-server/src/archive.rs `pub trait Archive` now carries both `store` and `list_keys`. The intake needs only store; rebuild needs only list. Every test double pays for the half it does not use: `UnavailableArchive` in tests/intake.rs got an `unreachable!("the intake never lists")`, and `Unlistable` in tests/rebuild.rs has the mirror image.

Fix: split into two traits (store seam, list seam), both implemented by FilesystemArchive and S3Archive; `rebuild` takes the list trait, `Intake` the store trait.
close_reason: Archive split into Store and List; doubles implement only the half their caller uses

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Split into Store and List. List is a for_each_key visitor, so rebuild folds the listing instead of holding it. No unreachable!() left in any double.

title: Prometheus scrape into a sample
description:
## What to build

The agent turns one scrape of the node's loopback PrometheusSimple endpoint into one sample: the 8 v1 fields, node version/revision parsed from the build_info labelled metric, every field nullable because a failed scrape is itself signal (ADR 0007). Fixtures are cassette recordings of real Leios node bodies replayed via wiremock, with a committed re-record script — so review can trust the parser matches Leios metric names, not stock cardano-node assumptions.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Recorded Leios scrape body in → sample with correct field values out.
- [ ] Unreachable endpoint or missing metric → sample with nulls, no error path taken.
- [ ] Hand-authored edge-case fixtures live visibly separate from recordings.
- [ ] Re-record script committed; fixtures documented to refresh on Leios flake-input bumps.

## Blocked by

Envelope and Ed25519 sign/verify core (sample type lives in the envelope).
close_reason: scrape into sample with real Leios cassettes; flake check green

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Shipped: scrape.rs turning one PrometheusSimple scrape into one Sample, infallible (failures degrade to nulls per ADR 0007). Metric names frozen against real cassettes recorded from a lone forging Leios node at the flake-pinned prototype tag; startup body doubles as the real missing-metric fixture. Hand-authored edge cases separate under edge-cases/. Re-record script scripts/record-scrape-fixtures.sh committed and exercised end-to-end. 9 wiremock tests; flake source filter keeps .prom files. Filed metsuke-ixn (sync_progress has no source metric); noted on metsuke-9a1 that its extraction trigger fired.

title: Server SQLite holds no envelope metadata, only counters
description:
ADR 0005 has the server SQLite as a rebuildable index of submissions. `crates/metsuke-server/src/counters.rs` MIGRATIONS holds only the `counters` table, and `intake::accept` writes no submission row, so the index records counter state and nothing else. `rebuild` reconstructs that much and no more.

Blocks metsuke-4zo.10 (developer data endpoints), which needs per-submission rows to serve.

Fix: decide whether the index gains a submissions table, and if so extend `rebuild` to populate it from the listing plus the object metadata headers.

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Re-frame: ADR 0005 already decided this, so it is not a "decide whether". Verbatim: "Envelope metadata (signature, key, counter, schema version) is stored twice: as object metadata headers and as a SQLite row. SQLite serves queries and the download endpoint". The S3 diff writes the four x-amz-meta-* headers and no row, so the index is counter state alone. Either implement the row (its consumer is the download endpoint, metsuke-4zo.10) or amend ADR 0005 — leaving both is silent ADR drift.

comments.author: claude
comments.text: ADR 0005 amended in the metsuke-4zo.7 diff rather than implementing the row: the Decision now says metadata rides as object headers and SQLite indexes whatever has to be queried (counters first, per-submission rows once an endpoint reads them). Drift closed, so this issue is now scoped to building the row with metsuke-4zo.10 rather than a decision. Amendment is one paragraph in docs/adr/0005 if it should be reverted.

title: Config accepts zero for every numeric field
description:
crates/metsuke-server/src/config.rs catches absence (no serde defaults, deny_unknown_fields) but not zero. `request_timeout_secs = 0` builds a ureq agent whose global timeout is zero, so every PUT fails and every upload becomes a 503. Same shape for `max_body_bytes = 0` and `rate_limit_window_secs = 0`.

The module header says "a missing limit is a deployment mistake, not a value to guess"; zero is the same mistake, uncaught.

Fix: NonZeroU64 where zero is never meaningful, or a ConfigError variant naming the field and the value it got.
close_reason: NonZero on every config field where zero is a deployment mistake

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Every field where zero means nothing is NonZeroU64/U32; put_retries stays u32 and says at the field why. tests/config.rs drives both loops off one field list.

title: S3 test doubles are hand-authored, never recorded from a real endpoint
description:
crates/metsuke-server/tests/s3.rs `FakeS3` plus the `FIRST_PAGE`/`SECOND_PAGE` ListObjectsV2 XML are written by hand. CLAUDE.md: "Test doubles are recordings ... A hand-authored stub erases provenance: nothing tells a reader which values were observed and which were guessed." Nothing in the suite has seen a real S3 answer, so a divergence in error-body shape, EncodingType handling, or presign acceptance is invisible.

`checks.test` is craneLib.cargoTest with no network, but a local server binary works: add pkgs.garage or pkgs.minio to nativeBuildInputs, run it on loopback, capture one PUT and one two-page listing, commit those as the cassette.

comments.author: claude
comments.text: This diff grows the surface: tests/s3.rs adds two more hand-authored `listing(..)` fixtures (`a_listing_that_never_ends_fails_at_the_configured_page_bound`, `a_listing_whose_token_does_not_advance_is_an_error`), both asserting continuation-token behaviour never recorded from a real endpoint. Whatever recording this ticket lands must cover the paginated ListObjectsV2 response, not just the single-page one.

title: hex() and the ureq agent builder are duplicated across both crates
description:
Three copies of `hex`: crates/metsuke/src/uploader.rs, crates/metsuke-server/src/s3.rs, crates/metsuke-server/tests/support/mod.rs. The lowercase-hex wire contract is documented in crates/metsuke/src/envelope.rs, which is its home.

Three near-copies of the agent wiring (`timeout_global(Some(..))` + `http_status_as_error(false)`): crates/metsuke/src/uploader.rs, crates/metsuke/src/scrape.rs, crates/metsuke-server/src/s3.rs. All three want the same "status handling is ours" agent.

The retry classification in s3.rs `answer` re-derives uploader.rs (2xx ok, transport + 5xx retryable, 4xx terminal), including the identical "unreadable reason: {error}" string.

Fix: pub fn hex and pub fn http_agent(timeout) in the metsuke crate; reuse the retry predicate and message, keep the outcome enums separate.
close_reason: one metsuke_wire::http for the agent builder and status split; hex was already shared

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Third copy landed in this diff: s3.rs hex() is byte-identical to metsuke/src/uploader.rs hex(). s3.rs unhex() is the same fixed-width decode loop as metsuke-server/src/http.rs decode_hex(), differing only in error type. Both belong to the one public helper this ticket adds.

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Third instance for this ticket, found in round 2 of the metsuke-4zo review: the `--config` value fetch (`args.next().map(PathBuf::from).ok_or(MissingValue)`) at crates/metsuke-server/src/cli.rs is already `fn value(args, flag)` in crates/metsuke/src/cli.rs. Reuse costs a `pub` plus a `flag` field on the server's `MissingValue`, against three duplicated lines — worth folding in only when this ticket touches the two cli.rs files anyway.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
The hex half is now partly done, and this ticket's prescribed home is stale.

metsuke-9a1 created `metsuke_wire::hex` (encode + decode::<N>), so "pub fn hex in the metsuke crate" in the body should read metsuke-wire. Gone: uploader.rs hex(), tests/support hex(), http.rs decode_hex()'s loop (now delegates).

Still open, and now divergent: s3.rs hex()/unhex() at crates/metsuke-server/src/s3.rs. unhex() calls u8::from_str_radix with no is_ascii_hexdigit pre-check, so it accepts a '+' sign pair ("+f" -> 15) that metsuke_wire::hex::decode rejects. Two strictnesses for one encoding. The doc comment 'Mirrors the header decoder in http' is also false now.

Unchanged: ureq builder x3, s3 retry classification, cli.rs value().

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Review of the uncommitted tree implementing this ticket's ureq-builder and s3-classification halves. No untracked files. All gates green in this session: `nix flake check` -> all checks passed; `cargo test --workspace` 196 passed / 0 failed; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- --deny warnings` silent; `cargo fmt --all --check` clean.

## In-scope

- crates/metsuke-server/tests/binary.rs:186 — fourth copy of the agent builder (`timeout_global` + `http_status_as_error(false)`) left behind by the extraction this ticket is. That file already imports `metsuke_wire` for `hex::encode`, so nothing blocks it. Fix: delete `fn agent()`, call `metsuke_wire::http::agent(Duration::from_secs(30))` at the one call site.
- crates/metsuke/src/uploader.rs:59-65 — unifying on the s3 predicate moves 1xx and 3xx from `Retryable` to `Rejected`. No data loss (main.rs:143 keeps the rows), but `Rejected` drives `schedule.rs:51`'s exponential backoff, so a stray 302 from a proxy now compounds the interval where it used to retry at the normal one. Verified: old code was `_ => Retryable`. Fix: keep it retryable in `classify` (`retryable: !(400..500).contains(&status)`) and drop the 3xx-is-terminal test, or record the change as intended — either way it is a behaviour change, not an extraction.

## Ticket record

- Comment 51's "Still open, and now divergent: s3.rs hex()/unhex()" is stale, and was stale before this diff: `git show HEAD:crates/metsuke-server/src/s3.rs` line 288 already delegates to `hex::decode`, as does `metsuke-server/src/http.rs:86`. Both are error-type adapters, not second decoders. The hex half is done.
- The ticket body says "pub fn http_agent(timeout) in the metsuke crate". The server cannot depend on `metsuke`, so the diff put it in `metsuke-wire`, which now carries a transport dependency. `lib.rs:1-6` was edited honestly to stop claiming the server links no HTTP client code, and the `Cargo.toml` comment states why TLS stays out. Recording the home change here rather than filing it; if metsuke-wire holding a transport dep is not wanted, that is a decision, not a fix.
- `cli.rs value()` (comment 36) stays deferred: this diff touches neither cli.rs.

## Beads hygiene

`.beads/issues.jsonl` is unstaged — `git add .beads/` in the same commit as the code. `CLAUDE.md` is also unstaged and its added line (`$CARGO_TARGET_DIR is set`) is unrelated to this ticket; land it separately or say it rides along. Ticket still `in_progress` with no resolution comment or close reason — pre-commit, your call. The map has no `## Decisions so far` section.

Filed: nothing. Every real finding is this diff's own work.

Verdict: two in-scope items, of which uploader.rs:59 is the only behaviour question. Everything else is green.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Round 2. Both round-1 fixes landed and are correct. Gates re-run in this session: `nix flake check` -> all checks passed; `cargo test --workspace` 196 passed / 0 failed; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- --deny warnings` silent; `cargo fmt --all --check` clean.

Three findings, all consequences of the F2 rule change. None blocking.

## Correctness

- crates/metsuke-server/src/s3.rs:135-148 and crates/metsuke-wire/src/http.rs:44 — `answer` now gives one condition two answers. `transient` lists `RedirectFailed | TooManyRedirects` as terminal, so a redirect the agent gave up on is not retried; `classify` returns `retryable: true` for a 3xx status, so a redirect that reached the caller as a status is retried `put_retries` times. Both land in the same `Failure.retryable`. Fix: decide which reading holds for a redirect and make the two agree — either drop the two redirect variants from `transient`, or exclude 3xx from `classify`'s retryable set.
- crates/metsuke/src/uploader.rs:26-28 — `Retryable`'s doc still says "Transport failure or 5xx", but after F2 a 1xx and a 3xx arrive there too. Fix: "Transport failure, or any status the server may answer differently next time — see `metsuke_wire::http::classify`."

## Diagnostics

- crates/metsuke/src/uploader.rs:59-61 — `classify` reads the refusal body to build `refusal.reason`, then the retryable arm discards it and reports the status alone. `main.rs:141` prints that string to the operator, so a 503's body is read and thrown away. Pre-diff the body was never read on this path, so it is not a regression — it is free information now available and dropped. Fix: `Retryable(format!("server answered {}: {}", refusal.status, refusal.reason))`.

## Verified, not a finding

- The s3 cost named in the fix note is bounded and visible: `store` at s3.rs:164-180 caps at `put_retries` with `put_retry_backoff` between attempts and logs each retry with the reason.
- `binary.rs` keeping the zero-arg `agent()` helper is right — four call sites, and its new doc states the case rather than the mechanism.

Verdict: the two uploader items are one-line edits; s3.rs:135 is the only one that needs a decision. Everything green.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Shipped metsuke_wire::http: agent(timeout) (timeout_global + http_status_as_error(false)) and classify() -> Result<(), Refusal>, replacing four agent-builder copies (metsuke uploader, scrape, metsuke-server s3, server tests/binary.rs) and the s3/uploader status split with its 'unreadable reason' string.

Decisions: home is metsuke-wire, not metsuke — the server cannot depend on the agent; ureq enters wire with default-features = false so the agent build does not inherit the server's TLS. A redirect is retryable everywhere now: classify treats non-4xx as retryable and s3::transient dropped RedirectFailed/TooManyRedirects, which previously read the same condition two ways.

Not done: cli.rs value() (comment 3). Sharing it across the crate boundary would put argument parsing in metsuke-wire for three lines, and the server has one flag whose message is already accurate. The hex half (comment 4) was already closed by metsuke-9a1 — s3.rs unhex and http.rs decode_hex are error-type adapters over hex::decode, not second decoders.

title: Server test fixtures re-authored per test file
description:
crates/metsuke-server/tests/support/mod.rs owns `submission()` but not its analogues, so each test file re-spells them:

- The `StoredSubmission` literal appears in tests/s3.rs `stored`, tests/rebuild.rs, tests/intake.rs (twice), tests/binary.rs.
- Two hand-rolled failing archives: `UnavailableArchive` in tests/intake.rs and `Unlistable` in tests/rebuild.rs.
- `CounterStore::open(dir.join("counters.sqlite"))` is spelled inline in tests/counters.rs, tests/intake.rs, tests/binary.rs and wrapped in tests/rebuild.rs.

Fix: `stored_submission(..)`, one parameterised failing archive, and a counter-store temp helper in tests/support/mod.rs.
close_reason: Server test fixtures moved to tests/support; the archive block is read from the shipped example

comments.author: claude
comments.text: tests/support gains stored_submission, counter_store, nonzero_*, FailingArchive, example_config and example_s3_archive. The hand-written [archive] block and the StoredSubmission literals are gone.

title: put_retries retries with no delay: add backoff, or drop server-side retry?
description:
crates/metsuke-server/src/s3.rs `store` re-issues the PUT immediately: the loop has no sleep, so the retry count is spent in microseconds. The failures it is documented for (503 SlowDown, transport reset) are exactly the ones that need backoff.

Q: add a configured `put_retry_backoff_ms` (CLAUDE.md: intervals are configuration, never constants), or drop `put_retries` entirely and let the client be the only retry layer, which ADR 0004 already makes it?
close_reason: Configured backoff between PUT attempts

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Decision: keep put_retries, add a configured put_retry_backoff_ms slept between attempts.

comments.author: claude
comments.text: put_retry_backoff_ms slept between attempts, asserted by a_failed_put_is_retried_up_to_the_configured_count_after_the_backoff.

title: request_timeout_secs is both the socket deadline and the presign lifetime
description:
crates/metsuke-server/src/s3.rs signs each URL with `self.request_timeout`, which is also the ureq global timeout. An operator tightening the ops timeout silently shrinks SigV4 signature validity to the same window, and clock skew against the endpoint then rejects every request with an error naming neither cause.

Q: split out a `signature_validity_secs` field, or keep one knob and document the coupling on it as a decision?
close_reason: Presign lifetime split from the socket deadline

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Decision: split out. S3Config gains signature_validity_secs; request_timeout_secs stays the ureq global deadline only.

comments.author: claude
comments.text: signature_validity_secs split out; request_timeout_secs is the ureq global deadline only.

title: Which clock owns last_seen after a rebuild?
description:
Live ingest writes the server receipt time: `crates/metsuke-server/src/intake.rs` calls `counters.reserve(pool_id, counter, now)`. Rebuild writes the object envelope timestamp: `crates/metsuke-server/src/rebuild.rs` calls `counters.reserve(name.pool_id, name.counter, name.timestamp)`. counters.rs documents last_seen as "the operator evidence of when a pool last got through", so after a rebuild that column is a client-claimed value bounded only by max_timestamp_skew_secs.

tests/rebuild.rs `the_summary_reports_each_pools_newest_object` asserts the envelope clock is intended, but the divergence from the live value is recorded nowhere authoritative.

Q: is last_seen the receipt clock (rebuild should write its own now) or the batch clock (ingest should write envelope.timestamp)?

title: rebuild-index reads an absent archive root as zero objects and exits zero
description: FilesystemArchive::list_keys maps io::ErrorKind::NotFound to Ok(Vec::new()), so `rebuild-index` against a mistyped or unmounted archive.root prints "rebuilt the index from 0 objects" and exits 0, leaving every replay counter unseeded. Same shape for S3: a wrong bucket lists empty. The NotFound branch is right for a fresh server; the ambiguity belongs to rebuild(). Fix: rebuild() refuses a zero-object listing unless the operator passes an explicit opt-in flag, so disaster recovery cannot silently no-op.
close_reason: rebuild-index refuses an empty listing unless the operator opts in

comments.author: claude
comments.text: rebuild takes EmptyArchive; a zero-object listing is refused unless --allow-empty. The error names the archive via the new List::location(), so the operator can tell a mistyped root from an empty one.

title: S3 list_keys pagination is unbounded and materializes the whole listing
description: S3Archive::list_keys loops on page.next_continuation_token with no page bound: an endpoint that returns the same token spins forever, silently, since request_timeout is per request. CLAUDE.md: limits are configuration, never constants. It also collects every key into one Vec before rebuild() folds it down to one ObjectName per pool, so the whole bucket listing is held in memory where a per-page fold would do (magnitude needs measurement). Fix: a configured max page count that fails naming the bound, and fold pages as they arrive.
close_reason: Bounded, folded S3 listing that cannot spin on a repeated token

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Same loop, second defect: `list_keys` never checks that the continuation token advances. An endpoint that returns the same `next_continuation_token` twice makes the loop run forever, so rebuild-index and verify-archive hang instead of failing — and a hang is worse than the unbounded Vec this ticket already covers.

Fix alongside the bounded-listing work: fail with `ArchiveError::List` when the new token equals the previous one, or cap pages at a configured maximum and error on exceeding it.

comments.author: claude
comments.text: list_max_pages bounds the listing and a non-advancing continuation token fails naming itself. Pages fold through the visitor, so no whole-bucket Vec. audit still materialises: its own cost is metsuke-4zo.37.

title: SNTP clock-offset probe
description:
## What to build

A per-sample SNTP query filling clock_offset_ms: single code path, configurable server list, shipped default time.cloudflare.com, null on probe failure. No timedatectl fallback — one path keeps the attack surface and the review surface small.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Offset computed from an SNTP exchange against a test server.
- [ ] Server list is configuration; default is time.cloudflare.com.
- [ ] Probe failure yields a null offset, not an aborted sample.

## Blocked by

Envelope and Ed25519 sign/verify core (field lives in the sample type).
close_reason: SNTP probe + sampler merge; scripted-UDP tests; flake check green

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Shipped: sntp module — hand-rolled RFC 4330 SNTP v4 over std UdpSocket (no new dep), probe(&SntpConfig) -> Option<i64>, servers tried in order, reply validation (originate echo, mode 4, stratum != 0, LI != 3, >= 48 bytes), failure -> None. Review round 1 added sampler::sample() owning scrape + probe + merge. Tests: 9 scripted-UDP-server SNTP tests plus a wiremock+UDP seam test; clippy deny-warnings, workspace tests, nix flake check all green.

title: The cold-key open sequence is typed twice: intake::accept and verify::verify
description: Both run the same ADR 0003 cold-key path: PoolId::from_cold_key(vkey) != pool_id refusal, then envelope::open with a match over envelope::OpenError into a local error enum. intake.rs maps into Rejection, verify.rs into VerifyError, so only the mapping differs. Fix: metsuke::envelope gains open_for_pool(vkey, wire_bytes, signature, pool_id, max_decompressed_bytes) with its own error enum; each caller maps that one enum into its rejection type.

title: No shipped server config example, so the S3 archive block has no operator-facing home
description: contrib/config.example.toml is the client only, pinned by metsuke/tests/config.rs example_config_documents_the_real_defaults. The server has no equivalent, so [archive] kind = "s3" with endpoint/bucket/region/request_timeout_secs/put_retries appears nowhere an operator can copy, and the ticket phrase "a configurable timeout and one retry" has no recorded value. Fix: contrib/server.example.toml plus a metsuke-server config test that loads it, matching the client convention.
close_reason: Shipped server config example, pinned by the config tests

comments.author: claude
comments.text: contrib/server.example.toml is the fixture every metsuke-server config test mutates, so a field the server grows must reach it before the suite passes.

title: S3Config.endpoint is a String, so a bad endpoint fails at first use not at config load
description: config.rs holds endpoint: String and S3Archive::new parses it into a Url, producing S3Error::Endpoint at startup rather than a config error naming the field. url is now a direct dependency of metsuke-server, so pub endpoint: Url deserializes through serde and makes the invalid value unrepresentable, deleting half of S3Archive::new error path. CLAUDE.md: make bad values unrepresentable.
close_reason: endpoint deserializes as a Url, so a bad one fails at config load

comments.author: claude
comments.text: S3Config.endpoint is a Url. What is left of S3Error::Endpoint is the bucket-construction case, covered by a_url_that_is_not_an_s3_endpoint_is_refused_at_construction.

title: Server dispatch matches (command, archive) as a cartesian product
description:
metsuke-server/src/main.rs `run` matches `(args.command, archive)`, so every new archive kind multiplies the arms by the subcommand count (four today, six with a third kind). Possible Repeated Switches. Compounding it, RebuildIndex reports via `report()` while the VerifyArchive arm inlines its printing and exit mapping.

Fix: match `archive` once into a generic `dispatch<A: Archive + Fetch>(archive, command, ...)`, and give the audit its own `report_audit`.
close_reason: Archive kind matched once into a generic dispatch

comments.author: claude
comments.text: run() matches the archive kind once into dispatch<A: Store + List>; the audit arm is the only per-kind difference and is the parameter. report_audit and report_rebuild are separate.

title: S3 GET body-read failures are marked retryable even when permanent
description:
metsuke-server/src/s3.rs `S3Archive::get` maps every `read_to_string` failure to `Failure { retryable: true }`. `ureq::Error::BodyExceedsLimit` and a non-UTF-8 listing are permanent; `transient()` next door excludes exactly those on the transport path. Latent today because nothing on the GET path inspects `retryable` — `list_keys` and `fetch` both take the first failure.

Fix: reuse variant matching as `transient()` does, or set `retryable: false` and say why at the site.
close_reason: S3 GET body-read failures are no longer blanket-retryable

comments.author: claude
comments.text: GET body-read failures classify through transient(), the same variant matching as the transport path.

title: rebuild-index fails closed on any key ObjectName::parse refuses
description:
rebuild::rebuild does `let name = ObjectName::parse(key)?;` per key, so one object under v1/ that to_key did not write — a hand-uploaded file, an ops marker, a lifecycle artifact — makes rebuild-index fail permanently with no way past it. tests/rebuild.rs `an_unparseable_key_fails_the_rebuild_naming_it` (the "stray-object" case) enshrines that as intended.

Fail-closed is defensible: seeding from a corpus you cannot fully read is how a counter goes backwards. But there is no override, and the operator running this has already lost their disk.

Decision: keep fail-closed, or collect refused keys into `RebuiltIndex.skipped`, seed from the rest, print them, and still exit nonzero?
close_reason: Decided to keep rebuild fail-closed on an unparseable key

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Decision: keep fail-closed, no override. The counter DB is backed up (metsuke-4zo.13), so a rebuild is not the only recovery path; an object the server did not write is news the operator wants loudly.

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Decided: fail-closed kept, no override. No code change; tests/rebuild.rs an_unparseable_key_fails_the_rebuild_naming_it holds it.

title: verify-archive opens and migrates the counter DB it never reads
description:
metsuke-server/src/main.rs run() does CounterStore::open(&counters_path)? before the archive match, so every subcommand pays it. verify_archive never touches counters, and on a filesystem archive the result is already known (Fatal::CannotVerifyFilesystem) — the SQLite file is created and metsuke::sqlite::migrate run purely to then refuse.

An audit against a host whose counters_path is wrong or unwritable fails naming the counter DB, which is not what the operator asked about.

Fix: pass &counters_path into dispatch and open inside the Serve and RebuildIndex arms only.

title: verify::audit fetches every object sequentially
description:
metsuke-server/src/verify.rs audit() loops `for key in archive.keys()?` and fetches one object per iteration. Each fetch+verify is independent — failures only accumulate into Audit.failures — so a full-bucket audit costs the sum of every S3 round trip.

Fix: fan the key list over a fixed worker pool (ureq::Agent is cheaply cloneable and shares its connection pool), merge (verified, failures) per worker. Pool width is a new [archive] config field, per CLAUDE.md (limits are configuration).

Magnitude needs measurement; the serialization is structural.

title: Second-valued config fields cast u64 to i64 unchecked
description:
ratelimit.rs RateLimiter::new does `time::Duration::seconds(window_secs.get() as i64)` and intake.rs accept does the same for `max_timestamp_skew_secs`. Both fields are NonZeroU64, so serde refuses zero but not a value above i64::MAX, which wraps negative: the rate limiter then treats every window as expired and never fires, and the skew check rejects every upload.

Reachable only by an absurd literal in the operator own config (the band is i64::MAX..u64::MAX), so no practical exposure. It is a finding because config.rs module header claims a value that means nothing is refused at load, and this class is not.

Fix: i64::try_from at load into a ConfigError naming the field, or hold both as NonZeroU32 seconds so the cast cannot wrap.

title: Decide whether the two Args::parse flag-value helpers share code
description:
crates/metsuke/src/cli.rs value() and crates/metsuke-server/src/cli.rs (inline, in the --config
arm) both take the next argv item as a PathBuf. Named for dedup in metsuke-9a1 comment 3, deferred
there: the parsers have different grammars and different ArgsError shapes, so the only shared part is
args.next().map(PathBuf::from) — a stdlib call. Recommendation: close as wont-do; sharing it adds a
metsuke-wire module that deletes no logic.
close_reason: wont-do: shared part is one stdlib call; a wire module around it deletes no logic

title: SQLite spool
description:
## What to build

The agent's only durability layer (ADR 0004): one rusqlite DB owning samples, delivery state, and schema migrations. Rows are deleted only on server ACK; all outstanding rows retry at startup and every upload interval; a configurable size cap bounds growth. Correctness here is what makes "nothing is lost across restarts or server downtime" true, so the tests are the review artifact.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Property test: write→ack→delete leaves no orphan rows in any state table.
- [ ] Restart with undelivered rows → they are offered for upload again.
- [ ] Size cap is configuration and is enforced.
- [ ] Schema migrations run on open; fresh DB and migrated DB behave identically.

## Blocked by

Envelope and Ed25519 sign/verify core (spool stores envelope samples).
close_reason: SQLite spool + delivery seam; all four acceptance criteria tested

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Shipped: spool.rs (SQLite durability layer: migrations via user_version, transactional push with configured max_samples oldest-drop, outstanding oldest-first, transactional ack, durable replay counter) and delivery.rs from review (take_batch seals outstanding rows into a SealedBatch holding row ids privately; ack consumes the batch). 10 tests incl. write→ack→delete orphan property test (mutation-checked) and restart durability.

title: upload_url accepts http://, sending signed telemetry in the clear
description:
crates/metsuke/src/config.rs:22 takes upload_url as a bare String; nothing rejects an http:// scheme. An SPO who drops the s uploads the signed body plaintext, and the agent reports a normal ack.

TLS is a hard requirement (docs/research/endpoint-protection.md, Transport).

Fix: validate the scheme when Config parses and fail loudly, the second option metsuke-b4r offered and did not take.
close_reason: upload_url is a validated newtype; plaintext off-host rejected at config load

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Review of the uncommitted tree implementing metsuke-4zo.40. Five tracked files, all staged, no
untracked files.

Gates run this session: `cargo test --workspace` 194 passed / 0 failed; `cargo clippy --workspace
--all-targets -- --deny warnings` silent; `cargo fmt --all --check` clean. `nix flake check` not
run.

Verified directly, not taken on report: `ureq::http::Uri` normalises the scheme, so `HTTPS://…`
parses to `scheme_str() == "https"` and is accepted (no case-sensitivity hole). `https:///v1/submit`
fails to parse outright rather than yielding an empty host, so the `Some(host)` check is not
bypassable. `is_loopback("[::1]")` is true, and `Uri::host()` does return the brackets, so the trim
is load-bearing.

## Intent — the loopback exemption, your decision

The ticket asked for the option metsuke-b4r offered: "bound the upload URL to https at config load
and fail loudly there." b4r names no exception, and endpoint-protection.md §4 Transport says "TLS
is a hard requirement regardless of payload signing" with no carve-out. ADR 0007's loopback
exemption is scoped to `metrics_url`, the scrape source, not the upload target. The diff adds a
second, undocumented policy: plaintext to any loopback IP literal.

It is not gratuitous. `tests/agent.rs:52` and `tests/uploader.rs:53` build `UploadConfig` from
`http://127.0.0.1:<port>` wiremock URIs, so without the branch the integration suite panics at
`try_into().unwrap()`. But `tests/config.rs:125` justifies it with "the integration suite and a
local reverse proxy both upload through" — the second half is invented. The repo's only reverse
proxy sits in front of the *server* (`metsuke-server/src/http.rs:3`, endpoint-protection.md:65),
not on the SPO host, and nothing documents a local proxy on the agent side.

So the exemption exists to keep the tests green, and the comment dresses it as an operator feature.
Three ways out: (1) keep it and record the decision in an ADR, dropping the reverse-proxy clause;
(2) keep it and cut the comment to the test-suite reason alone; (3) drop it, make `https`
unconditional, and give the tests a `#[cfg(test)]` or `pub(crate)` bypass constructor.
Recommendation: (2). The behaviour is defensible and the cheapest honest fix is to stop claiming a
deployment nobody has.

## In-scope fixes

- `src/uploader.rs:60-62` — `.map_err(|_| UploadUrlError::NotAbsolute(text.clone()))` labels every
  `Uri` parse failure as "must be an absolute URL with a host". Measured: `https://exa mple.org/v1`
  yields `InvalidUriChar` and `https://exa%zzmple.org/v1` yields `InvalidAuthority`; both are
  absolute and both have a host, so the operator is told the wrong thing. CLAUDE.md: a message
  naming what failed and what it got. Fix: a third variant carrying the `InvalidUri` as `#[source]`,
  or fold the parse error into the message.
- `src/config.rs:22` — `/// The metsuke-server submission endpoint (what it may be: \`UploadUrl\`)`
  names the field's own type back to the reader; the type is on the next line. Fix: restore the
  original one-line comment.
- `tests/config.rs:112-113` — "An operator who drops the \`s\` would upload the signed body in the
  clear and see a normal ack" is this ticket's body restated ("An SPO who drops the s uploads the
  signed body plaintext, and the agent reports a normal ack"). The ticket owns it and the
  `(metsuke-4zo.40)` pointer is already there. Fix: drop the sentence, keep the pointer.
- `tests/config.rs:125` — the reverse-proxy clause, per the intent section above.

## Design note, no change recommended

`crates/metsuke-server/src/config.rs:45` uses `url::Url` for `S3Config.endpoint` (metsuke-4zo.32),
so `UploadUrl` wrapping `ureq::http::Uri` diverges from the one URL-validation precedent in the
workspace, and `url::Host` would delete the bracket trim. Against switching: `url` is not a
dependency of the agent crate and adding it widens the static binary's tree against this repo's
smallest-attack-surface constraint, and validating with the same parser ureq dials with means there
is no second parse to disagree with the first. Keep `ureq::http::Uri`.

## Not findings, checked and dismissed

`UploadUrl` living in `uploader.rs` rather than `config.rs` (it is transport policy; `config.rs`
only borrows it via `serde(try_from)`, the same shape as `PoolId` from `metsuke_wire::envelope`).
Scheme case-sensitivity and the empty-host bypass, both disproved above.

## Filed

metsuke-4zo.42 — `metrics_url` is still a bare `String`, so nothing enforces ADR 0007's loopback
boundary. Same class of bug this ticket fixed for `upload_url`; no existing ticket covered it.

## Beads hygiene

`.beads/issues.jsonl` was staged before this comment and is dirty again from it plus the .42
filing — `git add .beads/` in the same commit as the code. metsuke-4zo.40 is still `in_progress`
with no resolution comment or close reason: pre-commit, your call. The map has no `## Decisions so
far` or `## Not yet specified` section, so nothing to graduate.

Verdict: not ready for /commit — the loopback-exemption decision is yours to make, and the three
prose fixes plus the mislabelled parse error should land with it. No gate is red and no behaviour
is wrong.

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Shipped: UploadUrl newtype in uploader.rs, only constructible via TryFrom<String>, requiring https or http to a loopback IP literal. Config.upload_url and UploadConfig.upload_url both carry it, so the invariant reaches .post(). Three error variants: Malformed (parser rejected it, carries InvalidUri as source), NotAbsolute (no scheme or host), Plaintext (scheme the agent refuses).

title: metsuke-server takes ureq's default features, so its TLS provider is whatever the next release picks
description:
crates/metsuke-server/Cargo.toml:29 is a bare `ureq = "3.4.0"`, so the server's transport takes `default = ["rustls", "gzip"]`. The agent (crates/metsuke/Cargo.toml) and metsuke-wire both spell theirs out with default-features = false.

Two consequences: a ureq release that changes its default provider silently changes the server's TLS stack, and gzip is pulled in for a client that only PUTs to S3.

Fix: default-features = false, features = ["rustls"] on the server too. Do not route ureq through a workspace table — metsuke-wire's manifest comment records why feature unification must not decide a binary's transport.
close_reason: server ureq names rustls; test-server gate guards it

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Review of the uncommitted tree implementing metsuke-4zo.41. Six tracked files, all staged, no untracked files.

Gates run this session: `cargo test --workspace` 234 passed / 0 failed; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- --deny warnings` silent; `cargo fmt --all --check` clean; `nix flake check` all checks passed, and `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.test-server .#checks.x86_64-linux.test-agent` both realise.

Verified directly, not taken on report: `ureq::Error::Rustls` is `#[cfg(feature = "_rustls")]` (ureq-3.4.0 src/error.rs:96-97), reached only through `rustls` -> `rustls-no-provider` -> `_rustls` in its Cargo.toml, so the manifest comment holds. `s3::transient` (src/s3.rs:136-149) also matches `Error::Tls(_)` and `Error::Pem(_)`, both `_tls`-gated; the comment names `Rustls` because that is the variant pinning this provider rather than merely some TLS, which is the right one to cite. ## Filed

title: metrics_url is a bare String, so nothing enforces ADR 0007's loopback boundary
description:
crates/metsuke/src/config.rs, field `metrics_url` (read by scrape.rs). ADR 0007 scopes the agent to the loopback Prometheus endpoint, but Config accepts any string: a typo'd or edited metrics_url pointing off-host scrapes a remote endpoint and the agent reports normal samples.

upload_url just got the `UploadUrl` newtype for the same class of bug (metsuke-4zo.40); metrics_url has no equivalent.

Fix: a validating newtype whose TryFrom requires http/https to a loopback IP literal, reusing the is_loopback check UploadUrl already has.
close_reason: metrics_url is a loopback-only newtype; endpoint.rs shares the check with upload_url

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Review of the uncommitted tree implementing .42. No untracked files; everything staged.

Gates run this session: `nix flake check` -> all checks passed; `cargo test --workspace` 260 passed / 0 failed; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- --deny warnings` silent; `cargo fmt --all --check` clean.

Intent is met: `metrics_url` is a validating newtype requiring http/https to a loopback IP literal, wired into `config.rs:21` and `scrape.rs:24`. Off-host, `localhost`, and `[::1]` are covered. Userinfo tricks (`http://127.0.0.1@evil.com/`) resolve to host `evil.com` and are refused. No silent-failure or reuse findings.

## Correctness

- `tests/scrape.rs:78-84` — `MetricsUrl` cannot hold 192.0.2.1, so the address had to change; but `127.0.0.1:9` refuses the connect immediately, which makes the 200ms `timeout` on the next line dead. TEST-NET-1 dropped packets, so that timeout was the mechanism under test. No scrape test now exercises the request deadline. Fix: rename to `refused_endpoint_yields_all_nulls` and drop the timeout override, then add a MockServer case that delays past the deadline. The .18 race does not return: port 9 is privileged and MockServer binds ephemeral ports, so nothing in the suite can claim it.
- `src/endpoint.rs:22-39` — `MetricsUrl` can never produce `Plaintext` and `UploadUrl` can never produce `NotLoopback`, so the shared enum is wider than either constructor. This is the cost of merging the two errors, which the ticket did not ask for (it asked only to reuse `is_loopback`). Fix: `MetricsUrlError` / `UploadUrlError` carrying only their reachable variants, with `absolute_parts` returning a small shared error each wraps. Keeping `is_loopback` and `absolute_parts` in `endpoint.rs` is the part that earns the new module.
- `tests/config.rs:164-185` — both new failure tests assert only that the message contains `metrics_url`, which all four variants do, so `metrics_url_naming_localhost_fails_loudly` would pass if `localhost` failed as `Malformed` instead of for being a name. The adjacent upload tests already assert the phrase (`:145`, `:158`). Fix: `contains("must be http or https to a loopback address")`.

## Prose

- `src/endpoint.rs:8-10` — "an endpoint off this host would have the agent sign another node's numbers as its own pool's (ADR 0007)". ADR 0007 argues privilege and attack surface and never states that reason, so the citation has a home but the sentence it carries has none. Fix: add it to ADR 0007's Consequences and cut this to "Loopback only (ADR 0007).", or drop the clause.
- `tests/config.rs:174-175` — points at `endpoint::is_loopback`, which is private and unreachable from the test crate. Fix: point at `endpoint::MetricsUrl`, whose doc carries the rule.
- `src/scrape.rs:23` — `E.g. \`http://127.0.0.1:12798/metrics\`` is a third copy of a value `contrib/config.example.toml:9` owns and `tests/config.rs:31` asserts. The type now names the constraint. Fix: delete the line.
- `tests/scrape.rs:79-81` — "being fixed it cannot be claimed" is a second copy of .18's body, and the actual reason for the change (`MetricsUrl` refuses off-host addresses) is stated nowhere. "Nothing binds the discard port" is a host property no artifact checks. Fix: `// MetricsUrl refuses off-host addresses, so this must be loopback; 9 is the discard port.`
- `src/endpoint.rs:1-3` — "each a type whose only constructor enforces its rule" restates `#[serde(try_from)]` plus the private field, both within 60 lines. Sentence two (they share the loopback test) is the real why. Fix: cut sentence one.
- `tests/config.rs:186` — restates `fn ipv6_loopback_metrics_url_parses`. Fix: delete.

## Beads hygiene

.42 is still `in_progress` with no resolution comment or close reason — pre-commit, your call. This comment makes `.beads/issues.jsonl` dirty again; `git add .beads/` in the same commit as the code. The map has no `## Decisions so far` or `## Not yet specified` section, so nothing to graduate. Nothing filed: every finding is this diff's own work.

Verdict: not ready for /commit — the dead timeout in scrape.rs is the one that loses coverage; the other five are cleanups.

title: TLS-handshake test helper is copied verbatim into both crates' tests
description:
opening_bytes and TLS_HANDSHAKE_PREFIX exist twice, byte-identical except pub and the Duration path: crates/metsuke/tests/uploader.rs:117-140 (written by commit c316d03) and crates/metsuke-server/tests/support/mod.rs:198-226 (copied by metsuke-4zo.41). Both prove the same thing, that the peer sees 0x16 0x03 on an https endpoint.

Also in both copies: `.expect("peer connected but sent nothing")` names a cause for what is any Read error (reset, read timeout). A true empty read returns Ok(0) and never reaches that branch, so the message is wrong exactly when it fires.

Decision needed on where a cross-crate test-only helper lives. O1: a module in metsuke-wire, the metsuke-4zo.23 precedent, but wire is linked into both shipped binaries and this is dead code there. O2: a new publish=false crates/metsuke-testsupport, dev-dependency only, no shipped surface. O3: leave both copies; 25 lines, two crates, no third caller in sight. Recommendation: O2.
close_reason: two copies kept deliberately; the misleading expect message fixed in both

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Decided O3: both copies stay. A new workspace crate costs a manifest, a member entry, flake.nix crateSrc entries and another gate derivation to deduplicate 25 lines of test scaffolding with no third caller; the copies can also diverge, since the server's budget comes from its TIMEOUT const. Fixed the finding that mattered: .expect("peer connected but sent nothing") fired only on a reset or read timeout, never on an empty read, so it now reads "reading the peer's opening bytes" and lets the io error supply the cause.

title: Client binary end-to-end
description:
## What to build

The complete agent an SPO runs: TOML config (pool_id, metrics_url, upload_url, optional signing_key; interval/SNTP defaults commented), key resolution --signing-key flag > config path > loud failure (systemd LoadCredential support), a 5-minute sample loop and a decoupled 1-hour upload loop (both configurable) that compresses, signs, and POSTs batches with pool_id/vkey/signature headers. 5xx or network failure keeps spooling and retries next interval with jitter; 4xx keeps the spool, logs the server's reason to journald, and backs off exponentially with a clamp; an ACK carrying a newer latest_version logs a journal warning. Demoable end-to-end against a wiremock server.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Recorded scrape bodies in → signed, compressed batch with correct headers out (external-behaviour test).
- [ ] Missing key at both flag and config → startup fails loudly.
- [ ] 5xx: spool intact, retry scheduled with jitter. 4xx: spool intact, reason logged, backoff clamped.
- [ ] ACK deletes the delivered rows; newer latest_version in the ACK logs a warning.
- [ ] Sample and upload cadences are independent configuration.

## Blocked by

Prometheus scrape into a sample; SNTP clock-offset probe; SQLite spool.
close_reason: client binary end-to-end; 32 tests incl. binary-level; flake check green

Delivery now takes pool_id from config (Calidus, ADR 0003). Review round 1: split AckAfterAccept error, binary-level tests incl. mutation-checked flag>config precedence, tests/support module, prose fixes. Filed metsuke-oqh.

title: Server ingest pipeline, cold-key path
description:
## What to build

The ingest server accepting its first authenticated submission end-to-end. Checks run cheap→expensive: allowlist → per-pool rate limit → Ed25519 verify over the compressed bytes → bounded streaming decompression (fixed arena) → replay-counter check — verification precedes decompression so only authenticated bytes reach the decompressor (ADR 0002). Cold-key identity is pure computation: blake2b-224(vkey) == pool_id (ADR 0003). Accepted submissions go to storage behind a trait with a filesystem implementation (the cargo-test seam); the ACK carries latest_version embedded from the client crate at build. Every limit is configuration, never a constant. Rejections carry a reason the client can log.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Valid signed batch in → stored object (raw bytes as received) + ACK with latest_version out.
- [ ] Each check rejects independently with a distinct reason: oversized body, unknown pool, rate limit, unauthorized key, bad signature, oversized decompression, unsupported schema version, envelope pool id not the submitted one, timestamp outside the window, stale/replayed counter.
- [ ] Property test: replay-counter acceptance logic (monotonic per pool, state in SQLite).
- [ ] Decompression never allocates beyond its configured ceiling.
- [ ] No check reads decompressed bytes before signature verification passes.

## Blocked by

Envelope and Ed25519 sign/verify core.
close_reason: Intake library green; HTTP wiring split to .16

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Review of .4 (O3): build ingest as one intake module — single entry point taking raw bytes + signature, returning accepted-envelope-or-rejection with one exhaustive error type; key store, counter store, archive as adapters behind it. Keeps the four-ADR ordering out of main.

comments.author: claude

title: S3 storage implementation and rebuildable index
description:
## What to build

The production storage trait impl (ADR 0005): one S3 object per accepted submission, raw signed zstd bytes exactly as received, key v1/<pool_id>/<date>/<unix_ts>-<counter>.json.zst, envelope metadata duplicated into x-amz-meta-* headers so the bucket is self-verifying. PUT is synchronous before ACK — no server spool — with a configurable timeout and one retry, then 503 so the client keeps spooling. The server SQLite row is only an index: an admin command rebuilds it from a bucket listing, making server disk loss recoverable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Object key and x-amz-meta-* headers carry signature, key, counter, schema_version.
- [ ] PUT failure after one retry → 503, nothing indexed, client-visible.
- [ ] Rebuild command reconstructs an equivalent index from a listing of the stored objects.
- [ ] Stored bytes are byte-identical to the received body (self-verifying corpus).

## Blocked by

Server ingest pipeline, cold-key path.
close_reason: S3 archive, rebuildable index, and the verify-archive read path
