comments.text:
Review of the uncommitted tree. Gates run this session: `cargo test --workspace` 143 passed / 0 failed, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` clean, `cargo fmt --all --check` clean. No untracked files; everything staged.

## Correctness

- src/archive.rs `to_key`/`parse` — `to_key` takes `self.timestamp.date()`, the sender offset-local date; `parse` rebuilds via `from_unix_timestamp` (UTC) and then hard-rejects on `name.to_key() != key`. Envelope timestamps keep the sender offset (rfc3339 serde) and intake only checks skew, so a `+02:00` batch is accepted and stored under a key `parse` refuses. `rebuild` propagates ObjectNameError, so one such object permanently wedges the whole rebuild. Verified: timestamp 1755039600 at +02:00 stores under 2025-08-13, parse says "timestamp 1755039600 is not in the 2025-08-13 folder". Fix: `to_offset(UtcOffset::UTC)` in `to_key`, or reject non-UTC at intake.
- src/s3.rs `answer` transport arm — every `ureq::Error` is marked `retryable: true`. The comment names connection refused/reset/timed out, but the arm also catches TLS verification failure, DNS NXDOMAIN and invalid URL: the config errors most needing an immediate report instead cost `put_retries × request_timeout_secs`. The 4xx/5xx split below it makes this distinction correctly. Fix: match the variants, mark DNS/TLS/URL non-retryable.
- src/rebuild.rs — a `Reservation::Replayed` outcome is dropped, but `summary.pools` still prints the counter found in the listing, not the counter the database holds. On a partial restore, main.rs prints a value the rebuild did not write, indistinguishable from one it did. Fix: carry the outcome into RebuiltIndex, print seeded vs already-ahead.
- src/archive.rs `list_keys`/`walk` — three ways to lose an error: `!self.root.exists()` treats a permission error or broken symlink as an empty archive (so a typo'd `archive.root` exits 0 having seeded nothing); `else if let Ok(key) = path.strip_prefix(&self.root)` has no else arm, silently dropping a key; `path.is_dir()` returns false on a stat failure, pushing an unreadable directory as an object key so the later error names the wrong cause. `to_string_lossy` additionally mangles a non-UTF-8 name into an error naming something not on disk. Fix: `fs::read_dir` with only NotFound as empty, `entry.file_type()?`, relative paths through the recursion, `to_str().ok_or_else(..)`.

## Coverage of the acceptance criteria

Holding, with evidence: key shape (tests/archive.rs `a_key_carries_the_pool_the_day_and_the_counter`), all four `x-amz-meta-*` values and their presence in `X-Amz-SignedHeaders` (tests/s3.rs), byte identity (`assert_eq!(put.body, wire_bytes)`), one retry with a 403 not retried, PUT synchronous before ACK (intake stores, then commits, then returns Ack).

- tests/s3.rs `a_put_gives_up_at_the_configured_timeout` proves nothing. The "stalled" endpoint is `stalling.recv().map(drop)`, and tiny_http sends an empty 500 when a Request is dropped unanswered, so the PUT is refused instantly; the assertion is `elapsed() < 10s` against `request_timeout_secs: 1`, which passes at any timeout or none. Verified: the whole s3 test binary finishes in 0.01s. Fix: keep the Request alive in the thread, assert elapsed brackets the configured 1s.
- tests/s3.rs FIRST_PAGE/SECOND_PAGE use `v1/pool1/...`, and `pool1` is not valid bech32, so `ObjectName::parse` rejects every key `list_keys` returns there — and the test only compares raw strings. Nothing joins an S3 listing to the rebuild, which is the exact seam ADR 0005 rests on; tests/rebuild.rs proves it against a filesystem walk instead. Fix: `pool_of(&test_key()).to_bech32()` in the fixture keys, assert parse succeeds on what list_keys returned.
- Criterion 2 (PUT failure → 503, nothing indexed) is untested for the S3 archive. The 503 and unspent-counter tests run against FilesystemArchive; the S3 side stops at `store()` returning an error. The mapping is variant-independent in http.rs, so it holds by construction, but `ArchiveError::Upload → 503` never executes.
- No test loads a `kind = "s3"` config into the binary, so `Credentials::from_env`, `Fatal::MissingCredentials` and the `S3Archive::new` wiring are unproven, and `rebuild-index` only ever runs against `FilesystemArchive::list_keys`. Fix: one binary test with kind = "s3" against a fake endpoint answering 500, plus a missing-credentials exit assertion.
- tests/s3.rs `a_put_that_keeps_failing...` scripts three 500 replies but `put_retries: 1` consumes two, so the third documents an expectation the test cannot hold. `an_endpoint_that_is_not_listening_is_an_error` asserts bare `is_err()`, which passes for any failure including a bad presign; the sibling tests assert the error names the key.

## Prose

- src/s3.rs header: "Requests are presigned rather than header-signed, so the credentials never leave this process." The reason is false — SigV4 header signing also sends only the key id and signature. The actual reason is that rusty-s3 returns a signed URL and ureq has no signing hook.
- deny.toml: "bundling the roots keeps the static musl builds free of a host CA bundle" claims a build that does not exist in this tree (metsuke-4zo.12 is open). Keep the license-and-crate sentence, drop the musl clause.
- ADR 0005 restated four times ("the index is disposable, rebuildable from a listing"): src/archive.rs twice, src/rebuild.rs header, tests/rebuild.rs header. The self-verifying-headers consequence three times: src/archive.rs, src/s3.rs, tests/s3.rs. ADR 0004 "the client keeps spooling" three times: src/s3.rs twice, src/config.rs. CLAUDE.md: prose records why, exactly once. Fix: rebuild.rs owns the first, the META_* constants own the second, the retry field owns the third; everything else is a pointer.
- src/rebuild.rs and src/main.rs carry the identical "operator compares the counts against what they expect in the bucket". Drop the main.rs copy.
- src/cli.rs `Command`: "(ADR 0005)" — the ADR says the index is rebuildable, nothing about a run-once command; "Serving is the default" restates `Args::parse` and is already asserted by the CLI tests.
- tests/rebuild.rs `the_summary_reports_each_pools_newest_object` doc names `last_seen`, but the test asserts `summary.pools[..].timestamp`. Name the field under test.
- src/config.rs and tests/config.rs both say "for a VM test or a single-host deployment", forward-referencing a VM test that does not exist yet (metsuke-4zo.14 is open).
- src/config.rs names AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID/AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, already the text of `Fatal::MissingCredentials`; the error string is the checkable artifact. "keyed exactly as S3 keys them" appears in both src/archive.rs and src/config.rs.
- Restating the next line, delete: src/archive.rs "What every object key starts with" over KEY_PREFIX and `walk`'s doc; src/s3.rs "The outcome of one request, with the body dropped."; src/cli.rs "The rebuild-index subcommand's name"; src/main.rs "without any dynamic dispatch"; tests/binary.rs "Run rebuild-index against this server's config, returning its stdout."

## Minor

- src/main.rs `dispatch` takes `listen` and `ingest`, which the RebuildIndex arm never uses. Match on the command before building serve-only values.
- src/s3.rs `Failure.retryable` is dead on the GET path — `list_keys` never inspects it. `answered` is a one-caller alias for `answer(sent).map(|_| ())`.
- tests/s3.rs: the "Port 0 never accepts" comment sits over `http://127.0.0.1:1`. `an_endpoint_that_is_not_a_url_is_refused_at_construction` calls `FakeS3::start(Vec::new()).config(1)`, spawning a real listener and thread for a test that sends no request — build the S3Config literal as the sibling tests do.

## Scope beyond the ticket

src/config.rs replaces `archive_root` with a tagged ArchiveConfig enum including a Filesystem variant: a breaking operator-facing config change no ticket covers the migration for. `Archive::list_keys` was added to the trait (see metsuke-4zo.19). `ObjectName::parse` gained a folder-versus-timestamp cross-check nobody asked for, and it is what makes the UTC defect fatal rather than cosmetic. ureq moved from dev-dependencies to dependencies and deny.toml allows CDLA-Permissive-2.0 for webpki-roots — both required by the transport choice, and the license addition is one crate, not a widening.

## Filed

metsuke-4zo.19 (Archive trait split), .20 (index holds no envelope metadata), .21 (config accepts zero), .22 (S3 doubles are not recordings), .23 (hex + agent duplication), .24 (test fixtures re-authored).

needs-decision: metsuke-4zo.25 — backoff between PUT retries, or drop server-side retry since ADR 0004 makes the client the retry layer? metsuke-4zo.26 — split signature validity out of request_timeout_secs, or document the coupling? metsuke-4zo.27 — does last_seen belong to the receipt clock or the batch clock?

## Verdict

Not ready to commit. Blocking: the non-UTC key defect, the vacuous timeout test, the unparseable listing fixture that leaves the S3-listing-to-rebuild seam untested, and the missing kind = "s3" binary coverage for criterion 2. The ticket also has no resolution comment and its body still says "one retry" where the code makes retries configuration.

- src/archive.rs:85 — `if prefix != "v1"` sits beside `pub const KEY_PREFIX: &str = "v1/"`. Fix: derive the comparison from the constant.

Five second copies, one *why* each. CLAUDE.md: prose records why, exactly once.

- "reported as empty it would reset every counter" — src/archive.rs `list_keys`, tests/archive.rs `listing_a_root_that_is_not_a_directory_fails_naming_it`, tests/rebuild.rs `an_unreadable_archive_fails_the_rebuild`. Owner: the archive.rs guard.
- why TLS — Cargo.toml "TLS included: the bucket is reached over HTTPS" and deny.toml "Reaching the bucket over TLS is not optional". Owner: Cargo.toml. deny.toml should say only which crate the license covers.
- rebuild runs once and exits — src/cli.rs `Command` doc and src/main.rs module header. Owner: main.rs. Drop the cli.rs sentence.

- src/main.rs:66 — `match (args.command, archive)` is the cartesian product; a third archive kind doubles the arms (possible Repeated Switches). Fix: match `archive` once into a generic `dispatch<A: Archive>(archive, command, ...)`.

Filed metsuke-4zo.28, .29, .30, .31, .32; commented on metsuke-4zo.20 and .23.

- src/main.rs:93-104 — `verify-archive` over a bucket that lists zero objects prints `verified 0 objects` and exits 0, indistinguishable from a verified corpus — and that exit code is what the comment at :98 says a monitor watches. src/verify.rs:92-94 already states the property as "empty `failures` on a **non-empty** bucket"; nothing checks the non-empty half. - tests/s3.rs:45 — `trim_start_matches(&format!("/{BUCKET}/"))` strips the prefix repeatedly. `strip_prefix(..).unwrap_or(..)` is what is meant.

title: Calidus verification path
description:
## What to build

The second key path (ADR 0003), letting SPOs keep cold keys off the telemetry box: the upload vkey must match the pool's registered Calidus (label 867) key, resolved by SQL against the Leios db-sync, highest nonce wins, an all-zero key (CIP-151 revoke) rejects. Resolutions cache forever; a verification failure triggers exactly one fresh lookup and retry, rate-limited per pool, so db-sync sees no per-upload load and key rotation still converges.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Upload signed with the registered Calidus key verifies; unregistered key rejects.
- [ ] Highest-nonce registration wins; all-zero key rejects the pool's Calidus path.
- [ ] Cache hit performs no db-sync query; verify failure performs one refresh then re-verifies.
- [ ] Refresh-on-fail is rate-limited per pool (limit is configuration).

## Blocked by

Server ingest pipeline, cold-key path.

title: Allowlist generation admin command
description:
## What to build

The admin command producing the participant gate: registration CSV ∩ active on-chain pool registrations carrying the matching CIP-20 label-674 key musashinet_incentives_application_code, queried from db-sync, emitted as (pool_id, code) pairs into Nix-managed server config. Codes are public and never treated as secrets; runtime stays db-sync-free on the cold-key path. The command is how operators onboard pools, so its output format is the server's allowlist input format by construction.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] CSV row with matching on-chain code → pair emitted; CSV-only or chain-only pools are excluded.
- [ ] Output loads directly as the ingest server's allowlist configuration.
- [ ] Emitted with a summary the operator can review (counts of matched/excluded).

Server ingest pipeline, cold-key path (defines the allowlist it feeds).

title: Slow request body stalls all ingest
description:
crates/metsuke-server/src/http.rs: serve() reads bodies on the accepting thread and tiny_http 0.12 exposes no socket timeout (ServerConfig is addr+ssl only; Request hands out no stream), so one client trickling a body blocks every pool until it gives up. read_body bounds size, not time.

Fix: front the server with a proxy that fully buffers request bodies, and bind loopback. Belongs with metsuke-4zo.12, which owns the NixOS modules and the hardened unit. If the endpoint is ever exposed directly, tiny_http has to go.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Same root cause, second cost: memory, not just time.

Any path that answers without reading the body (413 by Content-Length, 404, 405, header-decode 400) leaves the remainder unread, and tiny_http's EqualReader::drop drains it with a single `vec![0; remaining]` sized by the *declared* Content-Length (util/equal_reader.rs:66-85; the >1024 branch at request.rs:215). Request::drop runs it on the serving thread, and no public Request method lets you skip it (upgrade/into_writer/respond all drop self).

Measured, debug build, one header-only POST declaring Content-Length: 4000000000, answered 400: VmSize 347544 kB -> 4253796 kB, freed when the client closed. RSS stays ~4 MB (calloc zero pages) until the attacker actually sends bytes.

Consequence: under the hardened unit's MemoryMax/LimitAS (metsuke-4zo.12) this aborts the process. Fix is the same proxy body cap this ticket already names; the cap has to be enforced *before* the request reaches tiny_http.

title: Agent panics on an https upload URL: ureq has no TLS provider

Review of the uncommitted tree implementing metsuke-b4r. Three files, all staged, no untracked files.

## The ticket's own premise is wrong, and the diff's comment is right

metsuke-b4r says ureq 3.4.0 *panics* on an https URI with no provider feature. It does not, in this configuration. `WarnOnMissingTlsProvider` is chained only under `#[cfg(feature = "_tls")]` (ureq-3.4.0/src/unversioned/transport/mod.rs:381-395), and `_tls` arrives only via `rustls-no-provider` or `native-tls-no-default`, neither of which `default-features = false` turns on. `TcpConnector` opens a plain socket, then run.rs:404-407 returns `Error::TlsRequired`, which uploader.rs:45 maps to `Retryable`. Observed directly: run at HEAD, the new test sees a TCP connection carrying zero bytes and no panic.

So the Cargo.toml comment is accurate as written and needs no change. What needs correcting is the ticket body, in the resolution comment.

The fix itself is verified: `cargo tree -p metsuke -e features` now shows rustls + ring + webpki-roots.

- `crates/metsuke/tests/uploader.rs:117-118` — the test does not guard the regression under this repo's gate, so the claim "the agent's transport carries a provider, not just the workspace build's" is held by nothing. `checks.test` is `craneLib.cargoTest commonArgs` (flake.nix:136) with no `-p`, so ureq's features unify across the workspace and metsuke-server's bare `ureq = "3.4.0"` supplies rustls either way. - `tests/uploader.rs:126,131` — `accept()` and `read()` are unbounded, and `join()` after them. Not a hang today, because ureq opens TCP before answering `TlsRequired` (0.01s failure, above). It becomes one the moment metsuke-4zo.40 lands: rejecting a non-https scheme at config load means `upload` returns before connecting, `accept()` blocks forever, and `cargo test` has no per-test timeout. Fix: `listener.set_nonblocking(true)` polled to a deadline, or run `upload` in the spawned thread and accept with a timeout, returning an empty vec so the existing assert reports it.
- `tests/uploader.rs:141` — `let _ = upload(...)` discards the outcome while the comment above it claims "the outcome is a transport failure either way". Nothing checks that, so the test also passes on `Acked`. Fix: bind it and assert `matches!(outcome, UploadOutcome::Retryable(_))`. That also turns the hang above into a fast, self-describing failure.
- `tests/uploader.rs:126-134` — third hand-rolled `UploadConfig`, alongside `upload_config(&MockServer)` at `:50` and the copy at `:101-105`. Same pool_id derivation, same 5s timeout. Fix: `fn upload_config(base: &str, timeout: Duration)`, callers pass `&server.uri()` or the https literal.
- `tests/uploader.rs:127-129` — the 5-byte buffer is pretence: only `bytes.first()` is asserted, so a 1-byte read passes and a 0-byte read yields an empty diagnostic string. Fix: `read_exact` on one byte, or assert the whole record header.

Probe worktree carrying this round's files with `features = ["rustls"]` removed, `cargo test -p metsuke --test uploader`:

    thread 'an_https_upload_url_speaks_tls' panicked at crates/metsuke/tests/uploader.rs:165:5:

      left: None
     right: Some([22, 3])
    test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed. finished in 0.01s

`Ok(0)` is the regression path, so the message is now true: a connection arrived carrying nothing. The read-timeout panic is unreachable there.

`nix eval .#checks.x86_64-linux.test-agent.name` → `metsuke-agent-alone-test-0`; `.test.name` → `metsuke-workspace-test-0`. Distinct drvPaths. ## In-scope fixes

- `tests/uploader.rs:121-123` and `:170` — round-2 item 5 was applied inverted. The report said "The comment at the assert owns it; drop the clause from the `opening_bytes` docstring." The diff did the reverse: the assert-site comment is gone and the docstring kept "and drops the connection straight after, which fails the peer's handshake". So `matches!(outcome, UploadOutcome::Retryable(_))` now stands bare with its why 47 lines up inside a helper. Also, the code contains no `drop` — `stream` falling out of scope is Rust semantics, not a decision. Fix: cut the clause from the docstring, put one line above the assert.
- `tests/uploader.rs:151-152` — round-2 item 4 half-applied. The report's fix was `// An https upload_url must leave the host as TLS.` The second clause survives as a paraphrase: "the agent's transport carries a provider of its own" is the same why as `flake.nix:138-140` and `crates/metsuke-wire/Cargo.toml:19-20`. Fix: delete the clause.
- `tests/uploader.rs:142-145` — the remaining-budget recompute is scaffolding for itself. The `.max(Duration::from_millis(1))` exists only because std rejects a zero timeout, and the subtraction exists only to need the floor. The peer has already connected by this point, so `stream.set_read_timeout(Some(budget))` is bounded and deletes both. Fix that, and give the read a message that names the bound: `.expect("peer connected but sent nothing")` rather than `"read from the peer"`, which prints a bare `os error 11`.
- `tests/uploader.rs:124` — `Option` names nothing the caller uses: the sole call site is `.expect("nothing connected")`. Fix: return `Vec<u8>` and `panic!("nothing connected within {budget:?}")` in the elapsed branch. One fewer type, and the message finally carries the budget.

Prose trims, lower value: `:116` "content type 22 (handshake)" restates `0x16` in decimal and the const's own name — only `0x03` is non-derivable. `:121-122` "so a cleartext regression prints as readable text" is held by `String::from_utf8_lossy` at `:168`; what prose does not hold is the bare `5`, which is there because `"POST "` is five bytes — say that instead.

Cosmetic, your call: `flake.nix:142-147` gives one check two names, attribute `test-agent` and `pname = "metsuke-agent-alone"`. `metsuke-test-agent` would collapse them. And `peer.join().unwrap()` at `:164` displays a helper panic as `Any { .. }`; `resume_unwind` on the payload keeps the message, though the child's panic already prints to stderr, so this is close to free either way.

Raised again, rejected again: moving `features = ["rustls"]` into `crates/metsuke-wire`. That contradicts the decision recorded at `crates/metsuke-wire/Cargo.toml:19-20` — "what a binary's transport needs is its own choice, and feature unification would otherwise hand the agent the server's". Round 1 surfaced the same idea. Keeping the provider per-binary is the accepted position; no action.

Not a finding, checked: the single non-looping `read` into five bytes cannot realistically return fewer than two for a real ClientHello — rustls writes it in one `write_all` and loopback delivers it as one segment. Not a CI flake risk.

title: Cold-key check has two sites: intake and verify
description:
crates/metsuke-server/src/intake.rs submit() and src/verify.rs verify() both run the ADR-0003 key check followed by envelope::open. The primitives are shared (PoolId::from_cold_key, envelope::open); the ordering is not.

Matters for metsuke-4zo.8: the Calidus path has to join at both sites or a Calidus-signed object stays unverifiable in the archive while verifying fine on ingest.

title: Config errors under [archive] point at the table, not the field
description:
config.rs ArchiveConfig is #[serde(tag = "kind")]; serde's internally-tagged path buffers the table into a Content value and drops toml's spans. So request_timeout_secs = 0 reports 'TOML parse error at line 16 | [archive] | invalid value: integer 0, expected a nonzero u64' — no field name. [ingest] fields point at their own line and column.

Pinned by tests/config.rs a_refused_value_is_pointed_at_by_its_own_line, which asserts both halves.

Fix: represent the archive kind without an internally-tagged enum, or validate the block a second time with a spanned deserializer.
